title: How ETF investors are keeping sight of their long-term objectives, amidst wild market swings
transcript_text: We're back on halftime. I'm Christina Parts and I'm with your ETF edge. Headline risk has dominated the equity and commodities markets as of late. But in the ETF market, the impact has been a little bit more muted. Joining me now is John Davy, CIO to story a portfolio advisor. John, I'm going to jump right into the questions. You have the majority of equity markets in oil that are swinging hard every single day on headlines lately. Yet, you maintain that ETF investors especially should not lose sight of their own long-term objectives. Why is that? Well, I think geopolitical risk is something that the market, you know, historically can model out and look at the distribution of outcomes. So, you know, the research shows that, you know, typically markets do get past this point and then do go up over time. I think the bigger concern I have is more about what's going on in the private equity and private credit space where, you know, if you look at like, you know, Blackstone, KKR, Blue Owl, you know, some of these stocks are down, you know, 30, 40% in the last three months. I don't think that it's systemic at this point. So, we're looking at like, the spread between double B's versus triple C's. And that spread is around 750 basis points, which, you know, the range of the last two years, let's say, is, you know, 900 to 550 somewhere around there. But it's definitely worth keeping an eye on, for sure. So, if you're bringing a private credit, and I let's say my focus on our investors are longer-term horizons, are you saying avoid private credit or are you suggesting any other way? To put your money to work right now? Yeah, I think it's more about looking at, you know, where can you get the best return per unit of risk? And obviously that space is, is challenge to the point. You know, I think there's plenty of, I think the, our online thesis is that the US economy is still quite strong and between tax cuts, tariff cuts, rate cuts, you know, there's a good, there's plenty of opportunities. We just think it's not in the mag seven stocks. It's in, you know, the broader, you know, let's say, mid cap space, equi-weight space in some of these sectors, like industrials, energy materials, sectors that, you know, can benefit from like an elevated, you know, let's say, stagflation environment, which I think is also not a big risk in a marketplace more so than, you know, geopolitical. Thank you, John. Short and sweet. And remember, you can all find our content at etfedge.com.
